thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency & 5xx spike detected in /v1/generate after recent deploy (tag: canary-2026-03-14T22). Grafana: https://grafana.internal/r/redwood/serving?panel=latency (auto-attach) :rotating_light:
Sam K: i'm on it. oncall. seeing the alert, am pinging eng-runtime now.
Jess M: yep that deploy is the canary that changed multiplex/concurrency defaults. I was watching canary but the traffic shape shifted. p95 -> 800ms (baseline 120ms), p99 -> 3.4s, 5xx rate ~11% on gateway.
Kevin L: adding telemetry snippets: query in grafana: `sum(rate(http_requests_total{route="/v1/generate",status=~"5.."}[1m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{route="/v1/generate"}[1m]))` returns ~0.112.
Jess M: logs (truncated):
```
2026-03-14T22:03:10Z ERROR transport: connection reset by peer
2026-03-14T22:03:11Z WARN runtime: kvcache miss spike, pending requests queued (queue_len=512)
2026-03-14T22:03:12Z INFO serve: request timeout after 2.5s, route=/v1/generate, model=llama-70b
```
Sam K: looks like connection pool exhaustion + longer tails. This is affecting host-level timeouts upstream (gateway reporting 504s). Is this a config change to multiplex?
Jess M: yes, default_concurrency was increased from 8 -> 24 in canary to improve throughput. We didn't anticipate small queries that keep sockets open.
Oncall SRE: can we throttle traffic to canary or shift traffic back to previous model variant?
Kevin L: metrics show canary ~12% of prod traffic; the issue's effect is cascading because downstream KV cache misses are piling up. Two options: 1) rollback canary, 2) reroute traffic off canary. Rollback is fastest.
Sam K: agreed. initiating rollback. @deploy-bot can you perform a rollback of canary-2026-03-14T22? I need a timestamped audit.
deploy-bot: Received rollback request by Sam K for canary-2026-03-14T22. Issuing: `rwd deploy rollback --tag canary-2026-03-14T22 --group serving`
deploy-bot: Rollback started. Kubernetes rollout undo triggered for deployment=serving-api, namespace=redwood-prod (kubectl output attached).
Jess M: while rollback runs, temp mitigation: lowering keepalive and reducing max_concurrency for the canary pods via remote feature flag: `featurectl set serving.multiplex.concurrency 8 --scope canary` (applied).
Oncall SRE: i'm seeing 5xx rate drop already, p99 trending down. New metrics: p95 140ms, p99 220ms, 5xx 1.9% (1m window).
Sam K: nice. deploy-bot: confirm rollback finished?
deploy-bot: Rollback complete at 2026-03-14T22:07:34 UTC. Canary tag removed from traffic.
Product Ops: any customer-facing impact? We had a slight blip in request success rates around 22:03-22:07. I'll prepare a short note: some requests experienced errors/timeouts; rollback completed and full service restored; follow-up will include RCA.
Jess M: immediate next steps: open an incident ticket, capture full trace slices, run perf regression on multiplex change with synthetic load (short queries pattern). Also add a canary circuit breaker to limit concurrency per pod.
Kevin L: action items: (1) revert multiplex default in config repo (PR queued), (2) create synthetic that exercises many short-lived requests and run during canary, (3) add telemetry alert for connection_pool_wait_time > 200ms.
Sam K: leaving for postmortem. Handoff to Oncall SRE and Jess for root cause analysis. If anything regresses, page me.
Oncall SRE: acknowledged. I will own the incident timeline and postmortem. I'll collect logs, flamegraphs, and correlate KV cache misses with request tails.
Product Ops: sending notification to affected tier-1 customers and marking status page as: degraded briefly, resolved.
Jess M: saving command history and the offending config diff: `git show origin/main:configs/serving/multiplex.yaml` -> changed default_concurrency: 24
Sam K: good catch. Thanks team — nice quick rollback. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED (short-live): root_ts=1768181818 closed_ts=1768182155. Labels: rollback, timeout-regression, postdeploy.

-- thread notes --
- timeline covered: 22:03 alert -> 22:07 rollback complete.
- impact: transient customer errors (5xx/timeouts), brief increase in p95/p99, resolved after revert.
- follow-ups: configuration revert PR, broaden canary tests, add pooled-conn telemetry and guardrails.
- owners: Jess M (fix/tests), Kevin L (alerts/telemetry), Oncall SRE (postmortem).
